passages.source_text: πλὴν πολλοί εἰσιν τῆς πλάνης κήρυκες, ἕνα τὸν τῆς κακίας ἡγεμόνα ἔχοντες· ᾧ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας εἷς, ὢν καὶ αὐτὸς τῆς εὐσεβείας ἡγεμών, ἐν ἰδίοις καιροῖς τοὺς πάντας καθαροὺς εὑρεθέντας ἕξει προφήτας. ἡ δὲ πολλὴ τῶν πεπλανημένων αἰτία γέγονεν αὕτη, τὸ μὴ πρότερον νοῆσαι τὸν τῆς συζυγίας λόγον, ὃν ἰδία ὑμῖν ἑκάστοτε οὐ παύσομαι ἐκτιθέμενος κεφαλαιωδῶς· πολὺ γὰρ τὸ κατ᾽ εἶδος λέγειν. ὑμεῖς οὖν τῶν λεγομένων γένεσθέ μοι φιλαλήθεις κριταί.

τοῦ δὲ λέγειν ἄρξομαι ἤδη. θεοῦ τοῦ τὰ πάντα πεποιηκότος τὸ μέγα καὶ ἅγιον τῆς προγνώσεως αὐτοῦ πνεῦμα εἰ μὴ τῷ ὑπὸ χειρῶν αὐτοῦ κυοφορηθέντι ἀνθρώπῳ δῴη τις ἐγχέναι, πῶς ἔτι ἑτέρῳ τῷ ἐκ μυσαρᾶς σταγόνος γεννηθέντι ὁ ἀπονέμων οὐ τὰ μέγιστα ἁμαρτάνει; καὶ οὐχ οἶμαι αὐτὸν συγγνώμης τυγχάνειν, κἂν ὑπὸ νόθου γραφῆς κατὰ τοῦ πάντων πατρὸς δεινὰ νοεῖν ἀπατηθῇ· ὁ γὰρ εἰκόνα (καὶ ταῦτα αἰωνίου βασιλέως) ὑβρίσας τὴν ἁμαρτίαν εἰς ἐκεῖνον ἀναφερομένην ἔχει, οὗπερ καθ᾽ ὁμοίωσιν ἡ εἰκὼν ἐτύγχανεν οὖσα. ἀλλὰ (φησίν) ἁμαρτήσαντα κατέλιπεν τὸ θεῖον πνεῦμα. οὐκοῦν συνήμαρτεν. καὶ πῶς ὁ τοῦτο λέγων οὐ κινδυνεύει; ἀλλὰ μετὰ τὸ ἁμαρτῆσαι εἰλήφει τὸ πνεῦμα. ἀδίκοις ἄρα δέδοται. καὶ ποῦ τὸ δίκαιον; ἀλλὰ δικαίοις καὶ ἀδίκοις ἐπιχορηγεῖται. τοῦτο πάντων ἀδικώτατον. οὕτως πᾶν ψεῦσμα, κἂν μυρίαις ἐπινοίαις βοηθῆται, τὸν ἔλεγχον κἂν ἐν μικρῷ χρόνῳ λαβεῖν ἔχει.

μὴ ἀπατᾶσθε. ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν οὐδὲν ἠγνόει. ὁπότε καὶ ὁ δημοσία κείμενος νόμος, ἀλληγορίας ἐγκαλύμματι διὰ τοὺς ἀναξίους σκέπων αὐτόν, τοὺς ἀληθείας γλιχομένους ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἀναπέμπει λέγων „ἐξέτασον τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ ἐρεῖ σοι, τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους σου, καὶ ἀναγγελοῦσίν σοι“. τοῦτον ἐχρῆν τὸν πατέρα ζητῆσαι, τούτους τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους ἐπιζητῆσαι. ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐζήτησας τίνος ἐστὶν ὁ τῆς βασιλείας χρόνος, τίνος ἡ τῆς προφητείας καθέδρα, καίτοι αὐτοῦ ἑαυτὸν μηνύοντος τῷ λέγειν „ἐπὶ τῆς καθέδρας Μωϋσέως ἐκάθισαν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι· πάντα ὅσα λέγωσιν ὑμῖν, ἀκούετε αὐτῶν“. αὐτῶν δὲ εἶπεν ὡς τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς βασιλείας πεπιστευμένων, ἥτις ἐστὶν γνῶσις, ἡ μόνη τὴν πύλην τῆς ζωῆς ἀνοῖξαι δύναται, δι’ ἧς μόνης εἰς τὴν αἰωνίαν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν ἔστιν. ἀλλὰ ναί (φησίν), κρατοῦσι μὲν τὴν κλεῖν, τοῖς δὲ βουλομένοις εἰσελθεῖν οὐ παρέχουσιν.

διὰ τοῦτο (φημί) αὐτὸς τῆς καθέδρας ἐγερθείς, ὡς πατὴρ ὑπὲρ τέκνων, τὰ ἀπὸ αἰῶνος ἐν κρυπτῷ ἀξίοις παραδιδόμενα κηρύσσων, μέχρις αὐτῶν ἐθνῶν τὸν ἔλεον ἐκτείνων καὶ ψυχὰς πάντων ἐλεῶν, ἰδίου αἵματος ἠμέλει. μέλλοντος γὰρ αἰῶνος βασιλεὺς εἶναι κατηξιωμένος πρὸς τὸν νῦν ἐνπροθέσμῳ παρειληφότα νόμῳ τὴν βασιλείαν.... καὶ τὸ μέγιστον ὅπερ αὐτὸν λίαν ἐλύπει ἐστὶν τοῦτο ὅτι ὑπὲρ ὧν ὡς τέκνων τὴν μάχην ἐποιεῖτο, ὑπ’ αὐτῶν ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ ἐπολεμεῖτο. καὶ ὅμως ἠγάπα καὶ τοὺς μισοῦντας καὶ ἔκλαιε τοὺς ἀπειθοῦντας καὶ εὐλόγει τοὺς λοιδοροῦντας, ηὔχετο ὑπὲρ ἐχθραινόντων. καὶ οὐ μόνον ταῦτα ἐποίει ὡς πατήρ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς αὐτοῦ μαθηταῖς ὡς πρὸς ἀδελφοὺς ἔχοντας τὰ ὅμοια ποιεῖν ἐδίδασκεν. τοῦτο πατήρ, τοῦτο προφήτης, τοῦτο εὔλογον τὸ αὐτὸν ἰδίων τέκνων βασιλεῦσαι, ἵνα τῇ ἐκ πατρὸς πρὸς τέκνα στοργῇ καὶ τῶν τέκνων πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἐνδιαθέτῳ τιμῇ αἰώνιος εἰρήνη γενέσθαι δυνηθῇ. τοῦ γὰρ εὐλόγου βασιλεύοντος, ἐπὶ τοὺς βασιλευομένους ἀληθὴς χαρὰ περὶ τοῦ βασιλεύοντος γίνεται.

πλὴν ἐπὶ τὸν πρῶτον τῆς ἀληθείας ἐπάνειμι λόγον. ἐὰν τῷ ὑπὸ χειρῶν θεοῦ κυοφορηθέντι ἀνθρώπῳ τὸ ἅγιον χριστοῦ μὴ δῷ τις ἔχειν πνεῦμα, πῶς ἑτέρῳ τινὶ ἐκ μυσαρᾶς σταγόνος γεγενημένῳ διδοὺς ἔχειν οὐ τὰ μέγιστα ἀσεβεῖ; τὰ δὲ μέγιστα εὐσεβεῖ, ἐὰν ἑτέρῳ μὲν μὴ δῴη ἔχειν, ἐκεῖνον δὲ μόνον ἔχειν λέγῃ ὃς ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς αἰῶνος ἅμα τοῖς ὀνόμασιν μορφὰς ἀλλάσσων τὸν αἰῶνα τρέχει μέχρις ὅτε ἰδίων χρόνων τυχών, διὰ τοὺς καμάτους θεοῦ ἐλέει χρισθείς, εἰς ἀεὶ ἕξει τὴν ἀνάπαυσιν. οὗτος ἄρχειν τε καὶ κυριεύειν πάντων τῶν ἐν ἀέρι καὶ γῇ καὶ ὕδασιν τετίμηται· πρὸς τούτοις δὲ αὐτοῦ τοῦ πεποιηκότος τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὴν πνοὴν ἔσχεν, ψυχῆς ἄρρηκτον περιβολήν, ὅπως ἀθάνατος εἶναι δυνηθῇ.

context.translation_policy_text:
# Translation Stance

This document states the translation commitments that guide every
decision in the People's Open Bible. Declaring them is an act of
honesty: critics can assess our output against our stated
commitments rather than guessing at hidden biases.

> **Status: first draft.** This document will be refined as the
> project matures. Input and disagreement are welcomed via GitHub
> issues.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

## Contested terms

The following terms appear frequently and carry heavy theological
weight. Our default rendering and rationale are recorded here.
Per-verse variance is documented in the individual YAML files.

| Greek / Hebrew | Default English | Alternatives considered | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Χριστός *Christos* | Messiah where independently titular; Christ in the name forms "Jesus Christ" / "Christ Jesus" | Christ, Messiah | Preserves the title's Hebraic messianic meaning while using the recognizable conventional English personal name |
| κύριος *Kyrios* | Lord | LORD, Master | Matches covenantal and NT usage |
| δοῦλος *doulos* | servant | bondservant, slave | Uses reader-facing "servant" consistently; documents bonded-status and ownership nuance in notes/audit metadata |
| πίστις *pistis* | faith | faithfulness, trust | Main text: faith; footnote alternatives where contested |
| δικαιοσύνη *dikaiosynē* | righteousness | justice | Both renderings preserved in footnotes for Pauline passages |
| ἱλαστήριον *hilastērion* | atoning sacrifice | propitiation, mercy seat | Dynamic rendering for accessibility; alternatives footnoted |
| ἀγάπη *agapē* | love | charity (archaic) | Lexical cognates in source kept |
| σάρξ *sarx* | flesh (literal) / sinful nature (metaphorical) | — | Context-dependent; per-verse documented |
| μετανοέω / μετάνοια *metanoeō / metanoia* | reorient / reorientation; toward God where the context warrants making the destination explicit | repent / repentance (traditional); reconsider / change of mind in documented exceptions | See "Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)" below; do not homogenize regret, divine relenting, or distinct turning words |
| νήφω *nēphō* | clear-minded (most contexts); sober (where Paul explicitly runs the drunk/sober metaphor) | sober-minded | See revision notes in 1 Pet 5:8, 1 Thess 5:6 |
| יְהוָה YHWH | Yahweh | the LORD, Jehovah | Renders the divine name as a name. Where the NT quotes an OT YHWH passage using *Kyrios*, the NT verse retains "Lord" to preserve the Greek; the OT source verse uses "Yahweh". |
| אָדָם *adam* | man / humankind (context) | — | Context-dependent per usage |

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.

## Change log for this document

Material changes to this document are themselves commits. Prior
versions of the stance are preserved in git history.

- **2026-04-21:** Removed creedal affirmations (Apostles' Creed,
  Nicene Creed, Chalcedonian Definition) and replaced with a
  theological-stance section that declines specific creedal
  commitment. Translation philosophy and contested-terms table
  preserved unchanged; those are methodology, not creedal
  commitment, and the project actually runs on them. Added a
  "Translating into other languages" section stating POB's long-
  term intention to ship in every feasible major language, with
  the full revision pipeline and transparent supported-language
  disclosure. Per-verse YAML citing the old `doctrine_reference`
  values is preserved as historical record; those are not
  retroactively edited.
context.ambiguity_review_standard: Apply the supplied DOCTRINE.md ambiguity policy: a defensible contextual rendering may be used in the main text when material alternatives and the reason for the choice are preserved in notes. A unique or uncontested interpretation is not required. Distinguish (a) an unreadable or unverified source, omitted content, invented restoration, or a construction for which no defensible English can be given, from (b) ordinary lexical, attachment, or referent ambiguity faithfully preserved in English or explained with viable alternatives. The former blocks publication; the latter does not automatically block it. A note cannot excuse unsupported wording: the proposed main rendering must itself be defensible from the supplied Greek. Clearly printed gaps must remain gaps, not be filled by invention. Never change a verdict merely to achieve acceptance.
context.selected_edition_coverage_standard: Coverage is assessed against ALL SURVIVING WORDING AND PRINTED GAP MARKERS in the selected image-checked edition, not against unavailable words of a hypothetical complete original. A confirmed printed lacuna must remain an explicit gap in the English, retaining the exact number of printed dots (layout whitespace may differ), with a source-quoted note explaining that its content is unavailable and no restoration has been supplied. Such faithful representation can pass selected-edition coverage; it must never be described as recovery of the lost wording or an unbroken original. Distinguish this from missing scan pages, unverified ink, omitted surviving Greek, an unsupported English completion, or a translation that obscures the gap: those remain blocking. Neither this scope clarification nor a prior suggestion is an instruction to accept a draft; independently check every surviving clause, every gap, and every disclosure.

passages.text: Nevertheless, there are many heralds of error, all having one leader of wickedness. For that reason there is one herald of the truth, himself also the leader of piety, who in their proper times will have as prophets all who are found pure. The chief reason people have gone astray has been this: they did not first understand the principle of pairing, which I will not cease setting out for you separately, from time to time, in outline; for speaking point by point is a lengthy task. Therefore, be truth-loving judges for me of what is said.

lexical_decisions.chosen: For that reason there is one herald of the truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: The singular noun is implicit from the preceding κήρυκες; “for that reason” renders the causal ᾧ λόγῳ.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in their proper times
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase is taken with the prophets as referring to the respective times in which they appear; attachment to the singular herald is possible but less natural with the plural καιροῖς.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the principle of pairing
lexical_decisions.rationale: λόγος denotes an account or principle, while συζυγία is the work’s technical language for a paired relation; alternatives include “doctrine of the pairs.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: in outline
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adverb indicates a summary treatment by principal points rather than a full exposition.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πολὺ γὰρ τὸ κατ᾽ εἶδος λέγειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: for speaking point by point is a lengthy task
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατ᾽ εἶδος means treating the matter specifically or item by item, while πολύ indicates its considerable extent.

source_issues.issue: The printed form is morphologically unexpected in this adverbial position. It is interpreted as an orthographic form of the adverb meaning “separately” or “privately,” without treating the image-checked reading as an OCR error.

passages.text: I will now begin speaking. If someone refuses to grant that the great and holy spirit of the foreknowledge of God, who made all things, was infused into the man brought to term by his hands, how does the person who assigns it to another—one born from a foul drop—not sin most gravely? I do not think that person obtains forgiveness, even if he is deceived by spurious scripture into thinking dreadful things against the father of all. For anyone who insults an image—and an eternal king’s image at that—has the sin charged to the one whose likeness the image happened to bear. “But,” he says, “the divine spirit left him after he sinned.” Then it sinned along with him. And how is the one who says this not in danger? “No, he had received the spirit after he sinned.” Then it has been given to unrighteous people. And where is justice? “But it is supplied to righteous and unrighteous alike.” This is the most unjust thing of all. Thus every falsehood, even if supported by ten thousand contrivances, is bound to meet its refutation even within a short time.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ ὑπὸ χειρῶν αὐτοῦ κυοφορηθέντι ἀνθρώπῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: into the man brought to term by his hands
lexical_decisions.rationale: κυοφορέω carries a gestational image, here paradoxically associated with God’s hands; “formed by his hands” is smoother but would suppress that image.

lexical_decisions.chosen: refuses to grant that ... was infused
lexical_decisions.rationale: The construction has implicit agency around the active infinitive ἐγχέναι. The passive English keeps the spirit as what is infused without adding an explicit agent not syntactically stated; “grant that God infused” is a viable alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: by spurious scripture
lexical_decisions.rationale: νόθος marks the writing as illegitimate or inauthentic, and γραφή in this theological context can denote a purported scriptural writing; “spurious writing” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: and an eternal king’s image at that
lexical_decisions.rationale: καὶ ταῦτα is an emphatic idiom highlighting the especially serious identity of the image’s subject.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Then it sinned along with him
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound verb explicitly presents the spirit as sharing in the man’s sin, which is the reductio advanced by the author.

lexical_decisions.chosen: even if supported by ten thousand contrivances
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves μυρίαις as the image “ten thousand,” though it can idiomatically mean “countless,” and takes ἐπίνοιαι as devised arguments or contrivances.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν ἔλεγχον κἂν ἐν μικρῷ χρόνῳ λαβεῖν ἔχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: is bound to meet its refutation even within a short time
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἔχει with the infinitive expresses an assured outcome, and ἔλεγχος here is exposure or refutation.

passages.text: Do not be deceived. Our father was ignorant of nothing, since even the law laid down publicly, while concealing him beneath a veil of allegory because of the unworthy, refers those who yearn for truth back to him, saying, “Examine your father, and he will tell you; your elders, and they will report to you.” It was this father one had to seek, these elders one had to seek out. But you did not seek to learn to whom the time of the kingdom belongs, or to whom the chair of prophecy belongs, even though he disclosed himself by saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees sat on Moses’ chair. Everything they tell you, listen to them.” He said “them” because they had been entrusted with the key of the kingdom, which is knowledge. It alone can open the gate of life, and through it alone it is possible to enter eternal life. “But yes,” he says, “they possess the key, yet they do not provide it to those who wish to enter.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: our father
lexical_decisions.rationale: The designation is retained without inserting a name or capitalizing it, since the immediate wording does not make the referent explicit.

lexical_decisions.chosen: beneath a veil of allegory
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐγκάλυμμα is a covering or veil, and the law is depicted as concealing the father through allegorical presentation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: refers ... back to him
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀναπέμπω can mean send or refer someone back to another authority.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τίνος ἐστὶν ὁ τῆς βασιλείας χρόνος, τίνος ἡ τῆς προφητείας καθέδρα
lexical_decisions.chosen: to whom the time of the kingdom belongs, or to whom the chair of prophecy belongs
lexical_decisions.rationale: The repeated genitive τίνος asks whose these prerogatives are; the English supplies “belongs” for clarity without identifying the person.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they had been entrusted with the key of the kingdom
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive perfect of πιστεύω here means being entrusted with something, not merely believing it.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἥτις ἐστὶν γνῶσις, ἡ μόνη τὴν πύλην τῆς ζωῆς ἀνοῖξαι δύναται, δι’ ἧς μόνης
lexical_decisions.chosen: which is knowledge. It alone can open the gate of life, and through it alone
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main rendering takes the repeated feminine pronouns as referring to knowledge. Because πύλη is also feminine and nearer to δι’ ἧς, “through which gate alone” remains grammatically possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: But yes
lexical_decisions.rationale: The emphatic response concedes possession of the key before contrasting the refusal to provide it.

passages.text: For this reason, I say, he himself rose from the chair. Like a father acting on behalf of children, he proclaimed what had from eternity been handed down secretly to the worthy; he extended mercy even to the nations and had compassion on the souls of all, while disregarding his own blood. For he, having been deemed worthy to be king of the coming age, against the one who had now received the kingdom under a time-limited law.... And the greatest thing, which distressed him intensely, is this: those on whose behalf he waged the battle as for children were themselves fighting against him because of ignorance. And yet he loved even those who hated him, wept for those who disobeyed, blessed those who reviled him, and prayed for those who treated him as an enemy. He did not do only these things as a father, but also taught his disciples that they must do the same toward brothers. This is a father; this is a prophet; this is what is fitting: for him to reign over his own children, so that through the affection that goes from a father to children and the children’s heartfelt honor toward their father, eternal peace might be able to arise. For when the fitting ruler reigns, genuine joy concerning the ruler comes upon those who are ruled.

lexical_decisions.chosen: he himself rose from the chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: The wording continues the chair imagery of the preceding section; ἐγερθείς is rendered as physically rising rather than merely being raised up.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ ἀπὸ αἰῶνος ἐν κρυπτῷ ἀξίοις παραδιδόμενα
lexical_decisions.chosen: what had from eternity been handed down secretly to the worthy
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀπὸ αἰῶνος may also mean “from of old” or “from the beginning of the age”; “from eternity” retains the broad temporal force without supplying a starting event.

lexical_decisions.chosen: disregarding his own blood
lexical_decisions.rationale: The literal image is retained. It may refer to accepting the shedding of his blood or, more generally, neglecting his own life and safety.

lexical_decisions.chosen: under a time-limited law
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound denotes something governed by a fixed term or deadline; “under a law with a fixed term” is a more literal alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: were themselves fighting against him because of ignorance
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive verb depicts him as the object of their hostility, while ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ supplies ignorance as its cause.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῖς αὐτοῦ μαθηταῖς ὡς πρὸς ἀδελφοὺς ἔχοντας τὰ ὅμοια ποιεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: taught his disciples that they must do the same toward brothers
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἔχειν with the infinitive conveys obligation. The phrase πρὸς ἀδελφούς may instead characterize those receiving such treatment as brothers, but no additional object is supplied in the Greek.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦτο εὔλογον ... τοῦ γὰρ εὐλόγου βασιλεύοντος
lexical_decisions.chosen: this is what is fitting ... when the fitting ruler reigns
lexical_decisions.rationale: The repeated εὔλογος language can mean reasonable, fitting, or rightful. “Fitting” connects the claim that he should reign with the character of his rule; “when a reasonable ruler reigns” is also possible.

source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly four dots after βασιλείαν, leaving the preceding construction without its missing continuation. The English preserves all four dots and supplies no restoration.

This image-checked printed form appears to be an unassimilated or irregular spelling of the compound ordinarily written with μ before π. Its meaning remains recoverable, and the translation does not treat it as an OCR error.

passages.text: Nevertheless, I return to the first argument concerning the truth. If someone does not grant that the man brought to term by God’s hands has the Messiah’s holy spirit, how is he not committing the greatest impiety by granting that some other person, born from a foul drop, has it? Rather, he acts with the greatest piety if he does not grant that another has it, but says that that one alone has it—the one who, from the beginning of the age, changing forms together with names, courses through the age until, having reached his own times and having been anointed by God’s mercy because of his labors, he will have rest forever. That one has been honored with ruling and exercising dominion over everything in air, on earth, and in waters. In addition, he received the breath of the very one who made man—an unbreakable covering for the soul—so that he might be able to be immortal.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Messiah’s holy spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: χριστός functions independently as a title, so it is rendered “Messiah.” The genitive relates the spirit to the Messiah without deciding whether possession, identity, or source is foremost; “the holy spirit of Christ” is an alternative form.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ ὑπὸ χειρῶν θεοῦ κυοφορηθέντι ἀνθρώπῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: the man brought to term by God’s hands
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering retains the unusual gestational force of κυοφορηθέντι together with the explicit image of God’s hands.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς αἰῶνος ... τὸν αἰῶνα τρέχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: from the beginning of the age ... courses through the age
lexical_decisions.rationale: The repeated rendering preserves the source’s repetition of αἰών and its portrayal of movement throughout the age.

lexical_decisions.chosen: changing forms together with names
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both changing forms and corresponding names are retained without identifying particular manifestations not named here.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: διὰ τοὺς καμάτους θεοῦ ἐλέει χρισθείς
lexical_decisions.chosen: having been anointed by God’s mercy because of his labors
lexical_decisions.rationale: χρισθείς is rendered “anointed” to preserve its relation to the title Messiah, while διά with the accusative gives the labors as the reason; “on account of his toils” is an alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: has been honored with ruling and exercising dominion
lexical_decisions.rationale: The two infinitives preserve the distinction between governing and holding dominion as the honor granted to him.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν πνοὴν ἔσχεν, ψυχῆς ἄρρηκτον περιβολήν
lexical_decisions.chosen: he received the breath ... an unbreakable covering for the soul
lexical_decisions.rationale: The second phrase is taken in apposition to the breath. The genitive ψυχῆς may alternatively be rendered “an unbreakable covering of the soul,” but the context favors a covering bestowed upon and protecting the soul.

This document states the translation commitments that guide every
decision in the People's Open Bible. Declaring them is an act of
honesty: critics can assess our output against our stated
commitments rather than guessing at hidden biases.

> **Status: first draft.** This document will be refined as the
> project matures. Input and disagreement are welcomed via GitHub
> issues.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.
